scenario.title: The Windy Farmers Market
scenario.context: A bustling farmers market in the town center on a sunny but windy Saturday afternoon
scenario.description: Chihiro, the market organizer, is speaking with one of the vendors, Aiden, whose tent has just been uprooted by a sudden gust of wind, scattering his products everywhere. Aiden must now confront the immediate stress of the situation.
scenario.speaker1_persona: Calm, empathetic and solution-oriented, always looking for ways to help and support the vendors during the market
scenario.speaker2_persona_1: High EQ - Calm and constructive, understands the situation is not ideal but knows getting upset will not resolve the issue at hand
scenario.speaker2_persona_2: Low EQ - Easily frustrated and tends to lash out when under stress, prone to blame others for his misfortunes
scenario.speaker2_persona_3: Low EQ - Overwhelmed and panics under stress, struggles to think clearly and take appropriate action
scenario.speaker2_persona_high: High EQ - Calm and constructive, understands the situation is not ideal but knows getting upset will not resolve the issue at hand
scenario.speaker2_persona_low: Low EQ - Easily frustrated and tends to lash out when under stress, prone to blame others for his misfortunes

conversation.speaker: speaker1
conversation.text: Aiden, are you okay? That was quite a gust!

conversation.speaker: speaker2
conversation.text: Yeah, I'm fine, but my stall...it's all ruined.

conversation.speaker: speaker1
conversation.text: Let's not worry about that right now. We need to pick up your products before they blow away.

conversation.speaker: speaker2
conversation.text: I've spent so long setting up, and now it's all for nothing.

conversation.speaker: speaker1
conversation.text: I understand your frustration, but let's clean up first and then figure out what to do next, okay?

conversation.speaker: speaker2
conversation.text: You're right, Chihiro. No use crying over spilled milk, I suppose.
